component.name: Lightmorphic Text
component.summary: Manage your Espanso text expansions without editing YAML

description.p: Lightmorphic Text is a graphical front end for Espanso, the text expander. It reads the match files in your Espanso configuration, shows every trigger and its replacement in one searchable list, and lets you add, change and remove them through a plain form. Espanso is reloaded after each save, so a new snippet works the moment you finish typing it.

Files you have written by hand stay yours: comments, key order and formatting are left alone, and only the values you actually changed are rewritten. Snippets that use Espanso features Lightmorphic Text cannot represent — variables, forms, scripts — are listed and shown as they appear in the file, but never quietly rewritten.

If Espanso is not installed, Lightmorphic Text fetches the right build for your session from Espanso's own releases and sets it up in your home folder. Nothing is installed system-wide, so it works the same on an immutable system such as Fedora Silverblue or Bazzite as it does on Linux Mint or Ubuntu. On Wayland it walks you through the one permission step that needs your involvement.

ul.li: Search every trigger and replacement as you type
Add, edit and delete snippets through a form, never YAML
Comment-preserving writes, with an automatic backup of every change
Espanso restarted after each save, so changes take effect immediately
Guided first run for X11 and Wayland, including installing Espanso itself
Light and dark, following your desktop

description.p: The tray icon now appears on GNOME Wayland.
The tray icon now appears reliably on desktops with a tray.
The update dot is a plain coloured circle in every state.
Closing the window now minimises to the tray on desktops that have one (KDE out of the box, GNOME with the AppIndicator extension); elsewhere closing still quits.
The update dot turns blue when a downloaded update is ready, and its tooltips are clearer.
Espanso now learns your keyboard layout automatically on Wayland, so triggers using keys like # or @ work on non-US keyboards.
